preconditions.description: The number of distinct scores m is between 1 and 31 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= ai <= 30 for ai in a)
preconditions.description: Each score ai in the input set S is between 0 and 30 inclusive.
All elements in the input set S are distinct.

postconditions.expression: stdout == '=(' or (stdout.startswith(str(n)) and n >= m and n <= 31 and all(0 <= ai <= n-1 for ai in a))
postconditions.description: If no tournament exists, output '=('. Otherwise, output the minimal n (number of vertices) followed by an n×n adjacency matrix representing a valid tournament with scores whose unique values match the input set S.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(stdout.split()[i][j]) <= 1 for i in range(n) for j in range(n)) and all(int(stdout.split()[i][i]) == 0 for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: The adjacency matrix is binary (0 or 1) and has zeros on the diagonal.

postconditions.expression: all(sum(int(stdout.split()[i][j]) for j in range(n)) == sum(int(stdout.split()[j][i]) for j in range(n)) + 1 if i != j else 0 for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: The adjacency matrix represents a valid tournament (exactly one directed edge between every pair of vertices).

postconditions.expression: set(sum(int(stdout.split()[i][j]) for j in range(n)) for i in range(n)) == set(a)
postconditions.description: The multiset of vertex scores in the tournament matches the input set S (duplicates allowed in the tournament scores).

postconditions.expression: not any(n < k for k in range(m, 32) if exists_tournament_with_scores(a, k))
postconditions.description: The output n is the smallest possible number of vertices for which a valid tournament exists.
